column1: # limits_classes.tsv — cap name -> INDEXING | OUTPUT.  One row per cap, tab-separated, sorted by name.
# INDEXING caps bound what can EVER be found. A silent one is unrecoverable by the caller: no flag, no
# budget, no follow-up call gets the answer back, and the output reads as "none exists".
# OUTPUT caps bound what is SHOWN from what was found. A silent one is still a defect, but a --detail,
# a page or a second call can recover the answer.
# WHY A SIDECAR AND NOT A TAG IN src/. This file is a stopgap with a known expiry. The classification
# belongs beside the declaration — a trailing `// INDEXING` on the constant itself, read by
# limits_build.py the same way it already reads the note — because a sidecar keyed by name can go stale
# in a way an inline tag cannot. It is a sidecar today only because the round that produced the
# taxonomy was not the round that could touch src/. Migrate it inline and delete this file; the gate
# arm that requires every row here to name a LIVE cap is what keeps it honest until then.
# COVERAGE IS PARTIAL AND THE DOCUMENT SAYS SO. Only caps with a sourced classification are listed.
# Everything else renders as an em dash, which reads as "not yet classified" — never as "neither".
# Adding a row is a claim about what the cap bounds; make it by reading the call site, not the name.
